rationale: He voted yes on the Laken Riley Act and to take up the Secure America Act, both immigration measures that became law, which fits stopping open-border policies. No recorded vote in our data is about building the wall, so that half of the promise is not rated.

votes.explain: The Laken Riley Act is an immigration enforcement bill that became law.
This vote moved the Secure America Act, an immigration bill that became law, forward.

bills.explain: He sponsored the Build the Wall Now Act. A sponsored bill alone does not count as a kept promise.

rationale: No recorded vote is clearly about stopping spending or ending a recession, and what counts as 'the spending' is not defined in the ad. He voted yes on several large spending bills; we do not judge those as for or against this promise.

She voted yes on the 2025 law that extended the tax cuts and yes on the Rescissions Act, which cancelled previously approved spending. We found no vote for a tax increase. She also voted yes on annual funding bills, which we do not treat as contrary to this promise.

votes.explain: A yes vote on the 2025 reconciliation bill that extended tax cuts, consistent with opposing tax increases.
A yes vote on the final version of the same bill.
A yes vote on cancelling previously approved spending, consistent with opposing big spending programs.

rationale: She voted no on the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, a bill that restricts abortion care, which is consistent with taking her stated fight for reproductive freedom to Congress. This is the only reproductive-health vote in our data for her.

votes.explain: She voted no on this abortion restriction bill.

bills.explain: She also cosponsored a bill to expand abortion access.
